name: Bitur
catalog_citation: Rogers, Phillip G. 2021. The phonetics of Bitur. In Kate L. Lindsey & Dineke Schokkin (eds.), Phonetic fieldwork in Southern New Guinea (Language Documentation & Conservation Special Publication 24), 108-119. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press. http://hdl.…
catalog_quote: There is no lexical tone or contrastive stress in Bitur. Vowel length is not contrastive, but it seems to be the most salient prosodic feature of the Bitur word. Not all words have a long vowel, and generally words do not have more than one long vowel, the exception being cases of reduplication. ... Monosyllabic words are often (but not always) pronounced with a long vowel, and this may be related to a constraint on the minimal word in Bitur. Long vowels are found in both syllables of disyllabic words, but more often in the first syllable. ... For longer words, long vowels are found among interior syllables—that is, they are not found in initial or final syllables. All this considered, it is possible to analyze Bitur as having lexical (non-contrastive) stress of which the primary acoustic correlate is length. ... audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding passage is present verbatim in the Rogers 2021 PDF we hold/text at sec. 4 Prosody, pp. 114-115, exactly as cited. (2) Deciding source: a 2021 phonetic description with acoustic analysis by the language's primary documenter, published in a peer-reviewed LD&C special publication; Glottolog lists it as the only descriptive work on Bitur, and searches of Rogers' publication pages (Pitt, pgr179.github.io, UCSB), ELAR and general web turned up no grammar, dissertation, JIPA illustration or other prosody study. (3) The classification 'lexical' (non-strict) follows the author's own wording ('lexical (non-contrastive) stress of which the primary acoustic correlate is length', position not predictable in disyllables, interior in longer words); the the primary-stress rule already records the author's hedge and the positional tendencies. Nothing found suggests a different coding. (4) Only list of works to obtain
